title: Update on Food Security Strategy with Revised 2035 Fibre and Protein Production Targets
what_it_is: Update on Food Security Strategy with Revised 2035 Fibre and Protein Production Targets

sections.label: Local production food security targets
sections.summary: Local production is one of four Singapore Food Story 2 pillars, targeting 20% of local fresh vegetables, beansprouts and mushrooms, and 30% of eggs and seafood.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Local production is one of the food security pillars of the Singapore Food Story 2, complemented by three other pillars which are import diversification, stockpiling and global partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We want to work with our local farms to build up the capability and capacity to supply 20% of our local consumption of fresh leafy and fruited vegetables, beansprouts and mushrooms; and 30% of our local consumption of eggs and seafood.

sections.label: Meats, rice, poultry excluded
sections.summary: Meats are excluded from revised targets due to resource efficiency, land intensity and climate, while rice and poultry fall under import diversification and stockpiling.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Protein types such as meats are not part of the revised targets due to factors such as resource efficiency, land intensity and climate conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: What we are not intending to produce locally, such as rice and poultry, will be considered under other pillars of the Singapore Food Story 2 such as import diversification and stockpiling.

sections.label: Farm support and challenges
sections.summary: Singapore faces high energy costs and labour constraints, so farms are supported sustainably through capability development and the Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Of course, Singapore also faces other challenges, such as high energy costs, labour constraints, especially since farming is not exactly one of the more favoured jobs, as the Member was alluding to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: And therefore, I think in terms of how we support our farms, it has to be in sustainable ways, such as capability development, providing funding and schemes through our Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund.

sections.label: New farms triple yields
sections.summary: New farms using agri-tech and new technologies yield about three times more than traditional farms in Lim Chu Kang.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Today, if you compare their traditional farms, which are in Lim Chu Kang, and their new farms, I think you can see that the yields are about three times more than what they do in the traditional farms – using agri-tech, using new technologies, using new ways of doing things.

sections.label: Claimed 45 times yield
sections.summary: It claims to achieve up to almost 45 times the yield of traditional farms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: What it claims to do is to get up to about almost 45 times yield of our traditional farms.

sections.label: Days of self-sustenance question
sections.summary: A question asks how many days Singapore could sustain itself on local production alone under the new targets if food imports stopped completely.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The second is in relation to, especially for the food security and to help us better understand our food security situation, if Singapore's food imports were to stop completely, how many days could the country sustain itself on local production alone under these new targets?

sections.label: Singapore Food Story new goals
sections.summary: The speaker says the Singapore Food Story must be developed differently, with new goals of 20% for leafy and fruited greens and 30% for proteins.

sentences.text: And therefore, in the short term, I think what is required is really to think about how we develop the Singapore Food Story in a slightly different way.
So, we now set ourselves new goals, which is 20% through leafy and fruited greens, as well as the proteins for 30%, which I think we are already somewhat there for the protein side.

sections.label: Farm productivity statistics 2019 to 2024
sections.summary: Between 2019 and 2024, farm yield productivity rose 10% for vegetables, 17% for seafood and 50% for eggs.

sentences.text: If you look at the statistics between 2019 and 2024, the productivity of farms has increased in yield by 10% for vegetables, 17% for seafood and 50% for eggs.

sections.label: Four pillars of food security
sections.summary: The Singapore Food Story security plan should be reframed from local production supplying 30% of nutritional needs to four pillars of food security.

sentences.text: If you think about the Singapore Food Story security plan, I think we got to then reframe the thought that is more than just local production supplying 30% of our nutritional needs, to one of four pillars of food security: local production, import diversification, stockpiling and putting in global partnerships.

sections.label: COVID-19 supply chain disruption coping
sections.summary: During COVID-19 supply chain disruption, Singapore moved from just Malaysia to other countries such as Brazil.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We have seen how we have coped with the supply chain disruption during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We have gone from just Malaysia to other countries, such as Brazil.

sections.label: Minimum local sourcing requirements question
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry considered minimum local sourcing requirements for major retailers and food service operators to create guaranteed demand and commercial viability for farms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given that our local farms face structural disadvantages against cheaper imports, has the Ministry considered any form of minimum local sourcing requirements for major retailers and food service operators, even a modest starting quota, so as to create guaranteed demand and help farms achieve commercial viability?

sections.label: Free market principles for food
sections.summary: The speaker says the principle is free market principles, and it is not in the interest of consumers or the Government to fund or subsidise food products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Speaker, I think as a principle, we go with free market principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Ultimately, I do not think it is in the interest of consumers or the Government to fund or subsidise food products, just as we do not do it for energy costs nor petrol.

sections.label: Greenphyto selling to retailers
sections.summary: Greenphyto launched last month but began reaching out a year ago and already sells to about 75 Singapore retailers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As an example, while Greenphyto was just launched last month, a year ago, they have already started to reach out and they are already selling to about 75 retailers here in Singapore.
